projects.title: Spatiotemporal Hotspot Detection in NYC Taxi Data
projects.summary: Finding where and when NYC taxi pickups cluster, using Scala and Apache Spark.
projects.problem: NYC taxi trips provide a way to study how pickup activity varies across a city and over time. This project combined spatial joins with statistical hotspot detection to identify regions with frequent pickups and location–day cells with unusually high activity.
approach: Implemented spatial joins in Scala and Spark SQL to measure taxi pickup density across regions.
Mapped pickup coordinates and timestamps to a geographic grid with daily time intervals.
Computed Getis–Ord Gi* scores to identify unusually high pickup activity across nearby cells.
Used distributed aggregations and cached cell counts to rank the top 50 location–day hotspots.
projects.scope: Two analyses addressed different questions. Hot-zone analysis counted pickups inside rectangular regions. Hot-cell analysis assigned pickups to a geographic grid and daily intervals, then calculated Getis–Ord Gi* scores from neighboring cells. The Spark workflow cached cell counts and returned the 50 highest-scoring hotspots.
projects.takeaway: Neighborhood joins were a central processing challenge. Each cell had to be matched with nearby cells before its hotspot score could be calculated, making the cost of the join an important part of the implementation.

projects.title: Interactive Map of Dinosaur Records
projects.summary: Exploring 309 dinosaur records on a world map linked to a geological timeline.
projects.problem: This visualization brings together location and geological time for 309 dinosaur records. A linked world map and timeline let users select a period and see which records fall within it, making geographic patterns easier to compare across periods.
approach: Mapped geographic coordinates for 309 dinosaur records in linked D3.js world-map and timeline views.
Implemented a draggable time selector to explore geographic distributions across geological periods.
Used color to distinguish dinosaur types and animated map updates across locations and time.
projects.scope: D3.js connects the draggable time selector to the map markers. Moving or resizing the selection updates the records shown, with colors distinguishing dinosaur groups and animated transitions helping users follow the changes. Locations come from the supplied dataset and are plotted on present-day continents.
projects.takeaway: Keeping the map and timeline in one view allows users to compare records across periods without moving between charts. The map shows recorded locations rather than a reconstruction of prehistoric continents.

media.alt: Animated demonstration of the dinosaur map changing as the time selection moves
media.caption: Moving the time selector updates the records shown on the map

projects.title: Student Recognition from Classroom Videos
projects.summary: Recognizing students in uploaded classroom videos and looking up their academic records.
projects.problem: The application turns uploaded classroom videos into student names and matching academic records. A video upload starts face recognition, followed by a DynamoDB lookup and a CSV file containing the results.
approach: Implemented Python handlers for video recognition on AWS Lambda and OpenFaaS.
Queried DynamoDB for recognized students and generated CSV results for storage in Amazon S3.
Tested service integration and output correctness with a workload of 100 simultaneous uploads.
projects.scope: Python handlers connected video processing to student-record lookups and CSV output. The AWS version used Lambda and S3, while a second version ran OpenFaaS functions on a local Kubernetes cluster. The implementation work also included integration testing and documentation. Face recognition relied on an existing library.
projects.takeaway: Testing followed the full path from uploaded video to saved result. The workload of 100 simultaneous uploads checked how the services worked together and whether the expected output files were produced.

media.alt: Architecture linking S3 video uploads, Lambda face recognition, DynamoDB student data, and CSV results
media.caption: AWS architecture for video uploads, face recognition, student-record lookup, and saved results

projects.title: Facebook Comment-Volume Prediction
projects.summary: Comparing four regression models to predict how many comments a Facebook post will receive.
projects.problem: This project examined whether a Facebook post’s attributes and previous activity could predict the number of comments it would receive in a future time window. Four regression approaches were compared on the same prediction task.
approach: Evaluated Lasso, gradient boosting, random forest, and neural networks for comment prediction.
Scaled input features and applied PCA to reduce the prediction inputs to four components.
Compared prediction error and evaluation time across five variants of Facebook activity data.
projects.scope: The experiments covered five variants of the Facebook Comment Volume dataset. Feature scaling and PCA reduced the inputs to four principal components before fitting Lasso, gradient boosting, random forest, and neural-network models. Evaluation compared prediction errors and processing time.
projects.takeaway: Considering error alongside evaluation time provided a clearer comparison than accuracy alone. The analysis focused on the volume of comments, with no attempt to interpret their sentiment or content.

media.caption: Dataset overview adapted from the project presentation
